from websters dictionary: a political philosophy, movement, or regime (as that of the Fascisti) that exalts nation and often race above the individual and that stands for a centralized autocratic government headed by a dictatorial leader, severe economic and social regimentation, and forcible suppression of opposition

TL;DR: If you like Star Trek, go look at the Cardassians from Deep Space Nine. They're a very good example of a fascist society.

Fascism is a system in which the needs of the state are seen as more important than the needs of individuals. Because of that, it looks similar to communism in a lot of ways: The government becomes huge and invades nearly every aspect of daily life, the people are expected to conform socially and ideologically, and the police (secret or otherwise) spend a lot of time "dealing with" anybody who steps out of line - sometimes that means being sent to harsh labor camps for years, sometimes it involves summary execution and an unmarked grave, but it almost always means a policy of pervasive monitoring of the populace and the systematic use of intimidation.

The biggest difference is in the reason fascists and communists believe that the state should have so much power over individual lives. Communism says that everybody is equal, so nobody should be allowed to own anything and everybody has to share - the government just helps people learn to share with each other and makes sure everybody can work together. Fascism says that of course people aren't all equal: Some people are just better at running the world than others, and of course the best thing to do is to follow them because they know what's best for the general population - and of course that means other nations should submit to their rule, too.
